exactly_one_experiment: structured Mutation IR representability probe (zero-model, static)
why_largest_elimination_first: Architectures B and C (the current proposal) REQUIRE a declarative IR to cover normal agent mutation behavior; Architecture D exists largely as a hedge against IR undercoverage. A single static probe over the existing control-trajectory corpus decides whether the mandatory-IR path is even viable before any IR, runtime, or query tool is built. It also produces the heterogeneity inventory and the corpus the Phase 9 census needs, so it unblocks two later phases at once.
capability_gate_first: yes: coverage is a capability-preservation gate; efficiency questions are conditional on passing it
method_no_model_calls: locate the spreadsheet control-trajectory corpus (absent from this workspace; this location step is prerequisite zero)
parse Python via AST + inventory openpyxl/workbook operations mechanically
classify each mutation operation: trivially representable / representable-with-parameters / requires-richer-semantics (rubric in control_mutation_census.json)
report: coverage fraction of a minimal IR, heterogeneity inventory, concrete IR-killer examples

decision_rule.if_minimal_IR_covers_typical_behavior: B/C remain viable; proceed to H0-vs-H1 mutation-boundary experiment
decision_rule.if_systematic_IR_killers: mandatory IR is falsified; pivot to D (transparent interception) or A (hardened I/O) and re-scope L4 as capture/observer
decision_rule.if_corpus_unlocatable: report the research program as evidence-orphaned; no architecture decision is grounded until provenance is restored

cost: no model inference, no benchmark changes, no implementation; static analysis only
